title: First-year summative analysis of ChatGPT capabilities and ethics
summary: First-year apprentices complete a four-part summative assessment on ChatGPT code generation, argumentation, bias, and professional ethics. They iteratively generate Java and Pep/8 Assembly, test opposing written arguments, document their prompting journey, and critically evaluate workplace and educational implications.

sources.title: Incorporating Generative AI into Software Development Education
sources.evidence_quote: The first two parts of the assessment required interacting with ChatGPT to generate well-formatted and functioning code in Java and Pep/8 Assembly

context.discipline: software engineering, programming, and professional ethics

assessment.summary: Test ChatGPT's programming and argumentation abilities and critically evaluate its limitations, bias, and ethical implications.
student_actions: Prompt and refine Java and Pep/8 Assembly programs.
Prompt arguments for cryptocurrency sustainability and opposing positions on a chosen topic.
Document the prompting journey and analyze output rigorously.
Discuss professional and ethical implications in education and work.

student_role.description: ChatGPT interaction is required across programming and argumentation components.

grading.method: Rubric assesses prompt construction, rigor of output analysis and comparison, journey presentation, overall evaluation, and ethical analysis.
